statement: Solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y\cot x=\cos x$, given that $y=0$ when $x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$.
solution: The integrating factor is $e^{\int\cot x\,dx}=\sin x$. Then $\frac{d}{dx}(y\sin x)=\cos x\sin x$, so $y\sin x=\tfrac12\sin^{2}x+C$. At $x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $0=\tfrac12+C$, giving $C=-\tfrac12$ and $y\sin x=\tfrac12(\sin^{2}x-1)=-\tfrac12\cos^{2}x$. Hence $y=-\dfrac{\cos^{2}x}{2\sin x}$.
hints: Apply the condition $y(\pi/2)=0$ to fix the constant.
